planting.note: Plant after all frost danger has passed; in zone 9 plant March–May. ColorBlaze Velveteen is a tender perennial that can be overwintered as a houseplant or maintained in zone 9 where light freezes kill back stems but roots often resprout. Pinch flower spikes promptly as they appear to keep energy directed into foliage.

directions: Plant in partial shade to shade in moist, well-drained, fertile soil or container mix; ColorBlaze Velveteen produces broad, velvety burgundy leaves with hot pink centers on a densely branched, upright pillar habit that holds its shape without staking. Like other ColorBlaze series coleus, it is bred to hold color through summer heat and blooms very late in the season if at all, extending garden performance into fall. The series shows good resistance to downy mildew, making it a reliable alternative to impatiens in shaded beds and combination containers. In zone 9, afternoon shade helps prevent leaf scorch and keeps the pink centers vivid through the hottest months.

planting.note: Plant after all frost danger has passed; in zone 9 plant March–May. Big Red Judy is a vigorous, large-growing coleus that can be kept as a houseplant over winter or maintained as a tender perennial in zone 9. Pinch flower spikes and tip-prune young plants to encourage the dense branching that gives mature plants their full, shrubby form.

directions: Plant in full sun to shade in moist, well-drained, fertile soil or a large container — Big Red Judy is unusually adaptable to light levels compared to most coleus cultivars; the large, serrated, pointed leaves emerge burgundy in spring and deepen to a rich solid red for the rest of the season. Its bold, upright habit and substantial 3–4 foot size make it an outstanding 'thriller' for large mixed containers or a striking anchor plant in a shaded border, where its scale rivals tropical foliage plants like cannas. Because it tolerates more direct sun than many coleus, Big Red Judy is a good choice for transitional areas that get morning sun and afternoon shade in zone 9 gardens.

planting.note: Plant after all frost danger has passed; in zone 9 plant March–May. Alligator Tears is heat-tolerant and deer-resistant, performing as a tender perennial in zone 9 where light freezes kill back top growth but roots often resprout.

directions: Plant in partial shade to full sun in moist, well-drained, fertile soil or container mix; Alligator Tears has small, serrated, pointed leaves that stay a crocodile-green at the margins year-round with a creamy pale-yellow teardrop-shaped center streaking down the middle of each leaf. The compact, upright habit and fine-textured foliage make it a versatile filler in mixed containers and border edging, contrasting well against larger-leaved, darker coleus cultivars. Like other ColorBlaze series selections, it holds its color and habit through summer heat and resists bolting to flower. In zone 9, morning sun with afternoon shade produces the brightest yellow centers.

planting.note: Plant after all frost danger has passed; in zone 9 plant March–May. Keystone Kopper can be overwintered as a houseplant or grown as a tender perennial in zone 9. Remove flower spikes as they appear since blooming detracts from foliage quality.

directions: Plant in full sun to shade in moist, well-drained, fertile soil or container mix; Keystone Kopper produces small, serrated, pointed leaves in a uniform, solid coppery-bronze color that holds steady from spring through fall without fading. The compact upright habit works well as a 'thriller' in mixed containers or as a warm-toned accent threaded through a border of green and burgundy foliage plants. Like other ColorBlaze series selections it tolerates heat and sun well while still performing reliably in shade, giving it flexibility across different garden exposures. In zone 9, this coppery tone pairs particularly well with chartreuse and deep purple companion foliage.

common_name: Under the Sea Electric Coral Coleus
scientific_name: Coleus scutellarioides 'Under the Sea Electric Coral'

planting.note: Plant after all frost danger has passed; in zone 9 plant March–May. Electric Coral is part of the Under the Sea series bred for finely dissected, coral-like foliage; it can be overwintered indoors or grown as a tender perennial in zone 9.

directions: Plant in partial shade to shade in moist, well-drained, fertile soil or container mix; Electric Coral has deeply cut, undulating, lobed leaves that mimic the branching texture of reef coral, colored crimson-red with distinctive chartreuse edges and violet tinges. The dense, compact, mounding habit and intricate leaf texture make it a standout novelty foliage plant for shaded containers and border edges, where its coral-like silhouette contrasts sharply with broad-leaved companions like hostas and caladiums. Like other Under the Sea series coleus, it stays low and full rather than growing tall and leggy. In zone 9, consistent shade and even moisture keep the finely dissected foliage from scorching at the tips.

common_name: Heart to Heart Va Va Violet Caladium
scientific_name: Caladium bicolor 'Heart to Heart Va Va Violet'

planting.note: Plant tubers after all frost danger has passed when soil temperature is consistently above 65°F; in zone 9 plant April–June. Va Va Violet was the first violet-toned strap-leaf caladium introduced to the trade.

directions: Plant in shade to partial shade in well-drained, moist, fertile soil rich in organic matter; Va Va Violet is a strap-leaf caladium with elongated, lightly ruffled leaves that emerge violet in spring and mature to a bright violet-pink with deep pink veining and narrow dark green margins, sometimes showing tinges of white. It forms a compact, upright mounding clump that is well suited to container plantings and small shaded border groupings, where its unusual violet coloring stands out against the more common reds, whites, and pinks of other caladium cultivars. As a strap-leaf type it holds up better in light rain and wind than the larger, thinner-leaved fancy-leaf caladiums. In zone 9's heat, consistent soil moisture keeps the violet tones from fading.

common_name: Heart to Heart Raspberry Moon Caladium
scientific_name: Caladium bicolor 'Heart to Heart Raspberry Moon'

planting.note: Plant tubers after all frost danger has passed when soil temperature is consistently above 65°F; in zone 9 plant April–June. Raspberry Moon was named a Proven Winners Caladium of the Year selection.

directions: Plant in shade to partial shade in well-drained, moist, fertile soil rich in organic matter; Raspberry Moon is a fancy-leaf caladium with lush, heart-shaped leaves in a lime-green base color overlaid with bold, irregular blotches and splashes of dark green and raspberry pink that appear to swirl outward from the center vein. The upright mounding habit and large leaf display make it an eye-catching centerpiece for shaded containers or a mass planting under trees, where the bright lime-and-raspberry coloring reads well from a distance. Its vigorous growth and good leaf count give strong garden performance through the full summer season. In zone 9, filtered light and consistent moisture keep the raspberry splashes vivid without the leaves scorching.

common_name: Heart to Heart Clowning Around Caladium
scientific_name: Caladium bicolor 'Heart to Heart Clowning Around'

planting.note: Plant tubers after all frost danger has passed when soil temperature is consistently above 65°F; in zone 9 plant April–June. Clowning Around is a fancy-leaf Heart to Heart selection with textured, raised leaf margins.

directions: Plant in shade to partial shade in well-drained, moist, fertile soil rich in organic matter; Clowning Around has heart-shaped fancy leaves in a peachy-pink background with bright rose-pink veins, framed by a thick, textured, olive-green margin flecked with bright green speckles. The slightly raised, puckered edge gives the foliage an unusually dimensional, almost quilted appearance compared to flat-leaved caladium cultivars. Its upright mounding habit suits container displays and shaded border plantings where the unusual peach-and-rose coloring can be appreciated up close. In zone 9's heat, even moisture and dappled shade keep the textured margins from browning at the tips.

common_name: Heart to Heart Heart and Soul Caladium
scientific_name: Caladium bicolor 'Heart to Heart Heart and Soul'

planting.note: Plant tubers after all frost danger has passed when soil temperature is consistently above 65°F; in zone 9 plant April–June. Heart and Soul is a compact strap-leaf Heart to Heart selection well suited to smaller containers.

directions: Plant in shade to partial shade in well-drained, moist, fertile soil rich in organic matter; Heart and Soul is a strap-leaf caladium with elongated, ruffled leaves that are primarily white to soft pink at the center, veined in a muted greyed-purple, and dappled with dark red-purple spots, all framed by a wide, deep green border. The compact, dense, upright mounding habit stays smaller than many caladium cultivars, making it well suited to window boxes and small shaded containers as well as border edging. Its intricate spotted pattern and multi-tone coloring give it visual interest even at close range. In zone 9, filtered light and consistent moisture keep the delicate white-and-pink centers from bleaching out in the heat.

common_name: Heart to Heart Caribbean Coral Caladium
scientific_name: Caladium bicolor 'Heart to Heart Caribbean Coral'

planting.note: Plant tubers after all frost danger has passed when soil temperature is consistently above 65°F; in zone 9 plant April–June. Caribbean Coral has received garden performance awards as part of the Heart to Heart series.

directions: Plant in shade to partial shade in well-drained, moist, fertile soil rich in organic matter; Caribbean Coral is a strap-leaf caladium with elongated, lightly ruffled, heart-shaped leaves in a warm coral-pink color veined in a slightly deeper pink and edged in a bright green border, with occasional white flecking. The compact, dense, upright mounding habit makes it well suited to smaller containers, window boxes, and border groupings where its warm coral tone pairs nicely with cooler pink and white companion plantings. As a strap-leaf type its narrower, sturdier leaves resist tearing in wind and rain better than large fancy-leaf cultivars. In zone 9, dappled shade and steady soil moisture keep the coral coloring bright through summer heat.

planting.note: Plant tubers after all frost danger has passed when soil temperature is consistently above 65°F; in zone 9 plant April–June. Mesmerized is a fancy-leaf Heart to Heart selection bred for sun-or-shade versatility.

directions: Plant in shade to partial sun in well-drained, moist, fertile soil rich in organic matter; Mesmerized has heart-shaped fancy leaves in a brick-red base color with distinctive green edges and chartreuse tinges scattered through the interior, giving the foliage a warm, glowing effect. The compact, upright mounding habit works well in mixed containers and shaded borders, and its tolerance for a few hours of direct sun makes it more versatile than shade-only caladium cultivars for transitional garden spots. Its warm red-and-chartreuse coloring pairs effectively with green foliage companions for contrast. In zone 9, morning sun with afternoon shade produces the richest red tones while protecting the leaves from scorch.
